explanation: Venice began in 1932, as part of the city's art Biennale, and is often called the world's oldest film festival. Cannes was due to open in 1939, but war intervened.

claims.text: The first Venice Film Festival was held in 1932.
The first Cannes Film Festival was held in 1946.
The Venice Film Festival began as part of the Venice Biennale.
The Venice Film Festival is often described as the world's oldest film festival.
Cannes was due to open in September 1939, but the festival was called off when the Second World War began.

writerNotes: Cannes is the more famous festival, which pulls guesses toward it. Fourteen years apart, so the separation guard holds without exact days. Self-check 9.3. Lint: clean. Claims: every claim listed, risk at or above the C26 floor; the schema's riskReason list has no only or counterintuitive, so such claims carry the nearest listed reason. Datasets: no pinned dataset covers film or TV facts, so every high-risk claim here needs checker evidence from the web. Rival test: Arguing for Cannes: it is the best-known festival, but its first edition was delayed to 1946, fourteen years after Venice. Volatility: evergreen; no time words; nothing depends on events after mid-2026. Regional: two European festivals followed worldwide. Style: Oxford spelling, straight single quotes, plain hyphens, explanation of 30 words. Myths: claims screened against myths.json, no match. Mystery and encore: not applicable to a practice item. Doubts: none beyond the high-risk claims flagged for external evidence.
